tools.name: timeline

tools.name: social_search

tools.name: format
tools.description: Trình bày dữ liệu đã có thành văn bản.

tools.name: send
tools.description: Gửi một đoạn văn bản đi.

tools.name: policy
tools.description: Tìm trong tài liệu nội bộ.

tools.name: paper_text
tools.description: Lấy nội dung text của một bài báo.

tools.name: dedupe
tools.description: Remove duplicate items from an existing list of research results, keeping the first occurrence. Use when the user asks to remove duplicates from supplied or already-collected items. This tool does not search, fetch, summarize, or publish; do not use it to collect missing data.

items.description: The existing list to deduplicate. Preserve all supplied item fields. Items missing the compared field are kept.

by.description: Use url for duplicate links (default), ignoring www, trailing slashes, fragments and utm_* parameters. Use title only when the user requests title-based deduplication; title matching ignores case, accents and repeated whitespace.

tools.name: text_stats
tools.description: Count words, characters and sentences in supplied text. Use only on text already provided by the user.

tools.name: wiki_search
tools.description: Search Wikipedia for an encyclopedia topic, person, place or technology.

tools.name: export_report
tools.description: Save a research report locally as Markdown or JSON.

tools.name: data_calc
tools.description: Calculate summary, mean, sum, min, max or percentage change from numeric research data.

items.title: AI and your job: Threat or opportunity?
items.summary:
MOBILE, Ala. (WALA) - Artificial intelligence is becoming a bigger part of everyday life, raising questions about what the technology could mean for workers and their jobs.

Some economists believe AI poses a particular threat to entry-level and repetitive work, including call center, data entry and junior copywriting jobs, according to The Wall Street Journal. Those tasks may be easier to automate. [...] But AI could also create opportunities. A Bloomberg article points to potential job growth in construction and manufacturing as companies build data centers and produce the chips that power the technology. Some higher-skilled office workers could also benefit if AI helps them become more productive. [...] The long-term impact on jobs remains unclear, but workers can take steps to prepare. Exploring AI chatbots, writing assistants and other tools may help people find ways to work more efficiently and develop skills that complement the technology.

items.title: Opinion: AI cannot replace being human – The Battalion
items.summary: I understand the appeal. College is busy. Between classes, jobs, extracurriculars, leadership positions and trying to maintain some semblance of a social life, there are never enough hours in the day. AI makes things easier. It can generate an outline, rewrite a paragraph, summarize a reading or produce an entire essay before you have even finished your Celsius. But convenience does not necessarily facilitate education. [...] There is also something to be said about individuality. AI can generate an argument, imitate a writing style or suggest a creative direction, but our perspectives are developed through our own experiences, disagreements, mistakes and interpretations. The things that make our voices interesting are often the very things that cannot be neatly generated from a prompt. If we constantly rely on the same tools to tell us what to think and how to express it, we risk losing the differences that make [...] I am not asking anyone to abandon AI. I use it, and I recognize the benefits it provides. But I do think we need to become more conscientious about when we use it and what we are asking it to do for us. Let it help with the tedious tasks. Let it serve as a resource. But do not let it become a substitute for your own intellectual development.

items.title: 🚨🇺🇸 NVIDIA, CHINESE INTELLIGENCE & THE BILLION-DOLLAR AI CHIP TRAIL — WHAT ARE WE MISSING? 🇨🇳🔎
items.summary:
🚨🇺🇸 NVIDIA, CHINESE INTELLIGENCE & THE BILLION-DOLLAR AI CHIP TRAIL — WHAT ARE WE MISSING? 🇨🇳🔎

While headlines focus on NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang’s admitted extramarital affair, a potentially far more consequential national security investigation is unfolding.

Forget the personal scandal for a moment. FOLLOW THE CHIPS.

🔎 THE MEGASPEED CONNECTION

At the center is Megaspeed International, a Singapore-based AI infrastructure company and one of NVIDIA’s major customers in Asia.

Its former executive, Alice Huang, has reportedly been identified in U.S. intelligence assessments as an alleged Chinese intelligence asset.

But the questions extend beyond espionage.

💻 THE DIGITAL FOOTPRINT

An examination of Megaspeed’s publicly accessible website source code reveals references to additional hyperscale data center infrastructure, including a section labeled DC2 and descriptions of advanced power, cooling, and modular computing systems.

These clues raise questions about Megaspeed’s infrastructure partnerships, corporate connections, and the ultimate destinations of advanced American AI technology.

⚠️ THE NATIONAL SECURITY QUESTION

Investigative reporting has already identified historical Chinese ownership connections and raised concerns about whether NVIDIA processors could be diverted through Southeast Asian intermediaries.

Meanwhile, U.S. congressional leaders are demanding answers about foreign intelligence threats, export controls, and NVIDIA’s security procedures.

The central questions are simple:

Who ultimately controls the infrastructure? Who receives the computing power? And could restricted American AI technology be reaching entities connected to Beijing?

These remain questions under investigation—not established findings of espionage or illegal chip transfers.

🇺🇸 “America First AI leadership” is a national security asset. Following the money, ownership structures, and semiconductor supply chains matters far more than following celebrity scandal headlines.

🎙️ THE 17TH PERSPECTIVE | FOLLOW THE EVIDENCE. QUESTION THE NARRATIVE.

items.title: AI and your job: Threat or opportunity?
items.summary:
MOBILE, Ala. (WALA) - Artificial intelligence is becoming a bigger part of everyday life, raising questions about what the technology could mean for workers and their jobs.

Some economists believe AI poses a particular threat to entry-level and repetitive work, including call center, data entry and junior copywriting jobs, according to The Wall Street Journal. Those tasks may be easier to automate. [...] But AI could also create opportunities. A Bloomberg article points to potential job growth in construction and manufacturing as companies build data centers and produce the chips that power the technology. Some higher-skilled office workers could also benefit if AI helps them become more productive. [...] The long-term impact on jobs remains unclear, but workers can take steps to prepare. Exploring AI chatbots, writing assistants and other tools may help people find ways to work more efficiently and develop skills that complement the technology.

items.title: Opinion: AI cannot replace being human – The Battalion
items.summary: I understand the appeal. College is busy. Between classes, jobs, extracurriculars, leadership positions and trying to maintain some semblance of a social life, there are never enough hours in the day. AI makes things easier. It can generate an outline, rewrite a paragraph, summarize a reading or produce an entire essay before you have even finished your Celsius. But convenience does not necessarily facilitate education. [...] There is also something to be said about individuality. AI can generate an argument, imitate a writing style or suggest a creative direction, but our perspectives are developed through our own experiences, disagreements, mistakes and interpretations. The things that make our voices interesting are often the very things that cannot be neatly generated from a prompt. If we constantly rely on the same tools to tell us what to think and how to express it, we risk losing the differences that make [...] I am not asking anyone to abandon AI. I use it, and I recognize the benefits it provides. But I do think we need to become more conscientious about when we use it and what we are asking it to do for us. Let it help with the tedious tasks. Let it serve as a resource. But do not let it become a substitute for your own intellectual development.

🚨🇺🇸 NVIDIA, CHINESE INTELLIGENCE & THE BILLION-DOLLAR AI CHIP TRAIL — WHAT ARE WE MISSING? 🇨🇳🔎

While headlines focus on NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang’s admitted extramarital affair, a potentially far more consequential national security investigation is unfolding.

Forget the personal scandal for a moment. FOLLOW THE CHIPS.

🔎 THE MEGASPEED CONNECTION

At the center is Megaspeed International, a Singapore-based AI infrastructure company and one of NVIDIA’s major customers in Asia.

Its former executive, Alice Huang, has reportedly been identified in U.S. intelligence assessments as an alleged Chinese intelligence asset.

But the questions extend beyond espionage.

💻 THE DIGITAL FOOTPRINT

An examination of Megaspeed’s publicly accessible website source code reveals references to additional hyperscale data center infrastructure, including a section labeled DC2 and descriptions of advanced power, cooling, and modular computing systems.

These clues raise questions about Megaspeed’s infrastructure partnerships, corporate connections, and the ultimate destinations of advanced American AI technology.

⚠️ THE NATIONAL SECURITY QUESTION

Investigative reporting has already identified historical Chinese ownership connections and raised concerns about whether NVIDIA processors could be diverted through Southeast Asian intermediaries.

Meanwhile, U.S. congressional leaders are demanding answers about foreign intelligence threats, export controls, and NVIDIA’s security procedures.

The central questions are simple:

Who ultimately controls the infrastructure? Who receives the computing power? And could restricted American AI technology be reaching entities connected to Beijing?

These remain questions under investigation—not established findings of espionage or illegal chip transfers.

🇺🇸 “America First AI leadership” is a national security asset. Following the money, ownership structures, and semiconductor supply chains matters far more than following celebrity scandal headlines.
